question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3-(-2)xy?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(0,0)$,$(2,-1)$,$(-1,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(0,0)}=3-(-2)(0)(0)=3, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(2,-1)}=3-(-2)(2)(-1)=-1, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-1)}=3-(-2)(-1)(-1)=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.
